item.title: Coffee Clip Exact URL Ending

Center this exact URL in white: https://example.com/Go?ref=June — keep the capitals and punctuation exactly as typed, all on one line. Nothing else written anywhere.

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent any credits.** I can’t give you a verified credit quote: the connected tools don’t expose an account-balance check or a price estimator, and the video tool doesn’t list its credit rate.

**The most credit-efficient approach is:**
1. Generate only the **5-second coffee pour**, silent, vertical **9:16**, at the free-plan **480p** setting.
2. In a free video editor, append a **3-second black card** and center this exact text in white on one line:
   `https://example.com/Go?ref=June`

That produces the full **8-second clip** while spending generation credits only on the coffee footage. Adding the card locally costs **no Magic Hour credits** and preserves the URL exactly. Asking a video model to generate the text risks misspellings, altered capitalization, or extra writing.

**Cheaper alternatives**
- **Zero generation credits:** use your own coffee-pouring footage and add the card in a free editor.
- **Shorter:** reduce the pour to 3 seconds, plus the 3-second card—6 seconds total, changing your requested timing.
- **Smaller:** 480p is the lowest listed free-plan video resolution. Exporting smaller afterward won’t reduce generation credits.

I recommend the **5-second generation + manually added card**, but I won’t run it without a verified price and your approval.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
Use **Shotcut**, a free desktop video editor with no export watermark. Download it from **shotcut.org**. These steps use your own footage and **spend no Magic Hour credits**.

### 1. Set up a vertical project
- Open Shotcut and create a new project.
- Under **Settings → Video Mode → Custom → Add**, set:
  - **Width:** 480
  - **Height:** 854
  - **Frame rate:** 30 fps  
  This is a small, approximately 9:16 vertical export.

### 2. Add and trim the coffee footage
- Open your coffee-pouring video and drag it onto the timeline.
- Trim it to the **5 seconds** you want.
- For frame-accurate timing, keep exactly **150 frames** at 30 fps.
- If needed, apply **Size, Position & Rotate** to fill the vertical frame and crop to a close-up of the cup.
- Mute the track using its speaker/mute control.

Choose footage with **no visible labels, captions, or other writing**, since you want nothing else written anywhere.

### 3. Create the black end card
- Choose **Open Other → Color** and select solid black.
- Add it directly after the coffee footage on the same track.
- Set its duration to exactly **3 seconds**, or **90 frames**.
- Ensure the clips touch without overlapping. Don’t add a transition—the cut should happen at exactly **00:00:05**.

### 4. Add the exact URL
Select the black clip and add the **Text: Simple** filter. Paste this as a single line, with no quotation marks or line breaks:

```text
https://example.com/Go?ref=June
```

Set:
- **Text color:** white
- **Background:** transparent
- **Outline/shadow:** off
- **Horizontal alignment:** center
- **Vertical alignment:** middle

Make the text box span the frame, then reduce the font size until the entire URL fits on **one line**, with some space at each side. Ensure this filter is applied **only to the black clip**.

### 5. Export and check
- Choose **Export → H.264 / MP4** and export the timeline.
- Watch the exported file and verify:
  - **0–5 seconds:** coffee pouring, no writing.
  - **5–8 seconds:** plain black background with only the centered white URL.
  - **Total duration:** 8 seconds.
  - **No sound**, fades, or transitions.
  - The URL retains the capital **G** in `Go`, capital **J** in `June`, and the exact punctuation `://`, `/`, `?`, and `=`.
